/Issued 103 PM MST Wed Nov 11 2026/ 

 -Meteorological Overview:

A strong upper-level ridge builds overhead through Friday, 
driving temperatures well above seasonal averages with a few 
climate locations approaching daily records. Over the next couple 
of days, a weak to moderate pressure gradient will sustain breezy 
conditions across the Rocky Mountain Front and Central Plains.
However, as a powerful Pacific trough approaches the West Coast 
on Thursday, downstream amplification will pump the ridge axis and
associated surface high pressure well north into Canada, creating
a pattern resembling an omega block. As the surface high shifts 
northward, the cross-barrier gradient along the RMF relaxes, 
decreasing winds. Simultaneously, the shifting gradient reorients
to favor breezy conditions funneling through the valleys of SW 
Montana Friday and Saturday. 

The omega block pattern will be short-lived as a sequence of 
energetic low-pressure systems begins an assault on the West Coast
and especially the Pacific Northwest. This initiates the 
breakdown of our ridging through this weekend. By Saturday, the 
ridge axis shifts east into the Central Plains as Montana 
transitions to weak southwesterly flow aloft ahead of a weaker 
shortwave trough. Moisture with the weekend wave will be sparse, 
resulting in isolated chances of light precipitation largely 
focused across SW Montana and the Rockies. Temperatures will 
remain marginal, keeping snow-levels high above 7kft. The primary 
synoptic role of this initial system is knocking down regional 
heights and helping usher in some more seasonal conditions ahead 
of potential systems next week. 

Forecast confidence struggles heading into next week, with 
guidance pointing toward an increasingly uncertain yet active 
pattern. Rather than a singular high-impact storm, recent trends 
favor more of a split-flow setup early in the week, shunting the 
deepest moisture and strongest dynamic forcing to our south while 
ushering a return to near- seasonal temperatures across our 
region. Behind this initial transition, the broader pattern 
remains quite chaotic. While multiple weak Pacific waves are 
likely to traverse the region through the week, bringing periodic 
low-end chances for precipitation and mountain snow, ensemble 
spread remains very high, and no large or high-impact systems are 
favored at this time. -JR

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

High confidence surrounds the unseasonable warmth through Friday,
as well as the transition toward ridge breakdown and cooler 
temperatures this weekend. Confidence is medium to high (50-60%) 
that Saturday into Sunday will feature low-impact light 
precipitation largely across SW Montana and the Rockies. Snow 
levels will remain well above pass levels, and the scattered 
nature of the precipitation indicates most lower-elevation 
locations will remain dry. 

Confidence has lowered regarding any significant or high-impact 
storm system early next week. While there is moderate confidence 
in a return toward seasonable temperatures, model spread is 
substantial regarding how individual waves track and interact:

Scenario 1 (Active, Chaotic Pattern): A split-flow regime keeps 
the primary moisture tap and strongest dynamics displaced to the 
south, while a series of weaker northern-branch shortwaves cross 
the Northern Rockies. This brings periodic light precipitation and
minor pass-level snow chances, but overall impacts remain minimal.

Scenario 2 (More Amplified or Consolidated Wave): A shortwave 
digs more aggressively or consolidates into a broader trough over 
the Plains. This would allow a stronger push of Canadian cold air 
and wrap-around moisture into Central Montana, potentially 
introducing a brief window for more organized precipitation, 
though confidence in this evolution remains low. -JR
